name: Battle rifleman, SOVS (our own design)
about: Made by Tools/battle_units/soldier_sov.py on soldier.py. Metres; x forward, y right, z up. Paints: 0 tunic, 1 trousers, 2 boots, 3 lower, 4 straps, 5 helmet, 6 pack, 7 skin, 8 wood, 9 steel, 10 coat, 11 coat_dark, 12 leather, 13 blanket, 14 hoof (the eyes are painted as boots). near = LOD0, mid = LOD1, far = LOD2, all in the rest pose (arms 45 degrees down). Each point rides on bone `part` and, by `w2` (0 to 0.5), on bone `part2`. Skinning: a bone's turn G = G_parent * q (q from the clip, identity at rest; G of a bone with no track is its parent's), its head X = X_parent + G_parent * (head - head_parent + move), and a point p on it goes to X + G * (p - head). Quaternions are [t, w, x, y, z] in these axes (as Unreal's FQuat). Clips are in place: `stride` is the metres one loop covers; the game moves the unit. A mesh may carry `shade` per point (0 to 1, the wear and seam darkening): its colour is the paint's colour times shade; with no `shade` every point is 1. Dress: snow; paint by its colours below (they differ from the summer man's). The near glb carries COLOR_0, a darkening to multiply each paint by: wear 0.82, the snow suit greyed 0.85; the mid and far are plain.

stretcher_front.from: field_clips.py: this file's walk (motion capture), slowed and shortened, the arms keyed to the poles
stretcher_front.about: The front man of a two-man stretcher (the Stretcher prop, battle-models/ground-props), walking at about 0.75 m/s (stride 1.064 m a 1.42 s cycle), head down, the prop's grip.front.left/right in his fists: `grips` (his left fist then his right, every key, the root's frame, the game's axes; `mean` their average). Play stretcher_front and stretcher_rear on one clock (same phase, in step). Place the prop's root at the mean of the four fists less 0.14 m, head end (+x) toward the front man; then his root x = the prop's x + 1.1 - his grips' mean x. The carried man (carried_wounded) at the prop's `lie`. The rifle rides slung on his back.

stretcher_rear.from: field_clips.py: this file's walk (motion capture), slowed and shortened, the arms keyed to the poles
stretcher_rear.about: The rear man of a two-man stretcher (the Stretcher prop, battle-models/ground-props), walking at about 0.75 m/s (stride 1.064 m a 1.42 s cycle), head down, the prop's grip.back.left/right in his fists: `grips` (his left fist then his right, every key, the root's frame, the game's axes; `mean` their average). Play stretcher_front and stretcher_rear on one clock (same phase, in step). Place the prop's root at the mean of the four fists less 0.14 m, head end (+x) toward the front man; then his root x = the prop's x - 1.1 - his grips' mean x. The carried man (carried_wounded) at the prop's `lie`. The rifle rides slung on his back.

splice_kneel.from: field_clips.py: kneel_down's last pose, the arms keyed
splice_kneel.about: The lineman at a cut wire, kneeling (kneel_down, then this, then stand_up), twisting the two ends together in his hands three times and giving it a tug (event wire_tug) to test it. The wire's two ends run into his fists at `hands` (left then right, the root's frame, the game's axes): draw each end from there down to the ground and away along the line. His reel sits on the ground by his right knee. The rifle rides slung on his back.

carried_wounded.about: The man on the stretcher, alive (the dead stay still; he does not): on his back, head to +x (the Stretcher prop's head end, carried first), breathing, his left knee drawn up and let down, his right hand on his chest, his head turning now and then. His root goes at the prop's `lie` socket, turned with it. No weapon (the weapon bone rides 2 m under his root). His white field dressing is the game's to place.

reel_walk.from: field_clips.py: this file's walk (motion capture), slowed and shortened, bent, the arms keyed to the reel
reel_walk.about: The lineman walking his line out, about 0.75 m/s (stride 1.064 m a 1.42 s cycle), bent forward, the CableReel prop (battle-models/ground-props) carried before him by its two handles: `reel` gives, every key, the prop's root (x, y, z) and his left and right fists (on its grip.left and grip.right), the root's frame, the game's axes; the prop faces as he does. Turn its drum by the wire paid out (the prop's README). The rifle rides slung on his back.

wounded_waiting.about: A wounded man on the ground waiting for the bearers, alive: on his back (head to +x, his root on the ground under his middle), breathing hard, his right hand pressed to the wound at his right side, his left knee drawn up and let down, his head turning, and once a loop his left arm lifted to call them. His rifle lies by his right side. When the bearers reach him: carried_wounded on the stretcher (the same lie, so it swaps without a jump but for the hands).

helmets.about: Gone grey and stained in the folds within weeks.

about_variety: Variety (Tools/battle_units/variety.py and helmet_finishes.py): one man made into many. `faces` (8): face 0 is the man as he is; for face k, add `move` (metres, this file's axes) to the points listed in `at`, at each level of detail, then colour: every skin-painted point's colour times `tone`, and each point in `tint_at` times its `tint` (the hair, brows, stubble or moustache), all on top of the paint (and `shade`) as usual. `helmets`: his helmet (or cap, ushanka or hood) in the finishes it was worn in. Each is a rigid mesh at near/mid/far in the same form as the file's own meshes (points, facings, paints, triangles, part, part2, w2, and shade where the file has it), with `ink` at each point: -1 paints the point by its paint number as ever; any other value is an index into `inks` (colours, RRGGBB), the colour to paint it instead. To draw a man in a finish, leave out his own helmet's triangles, `helmet_tris[lod]` = [first, count] (they are the last of the list), and draw the finish's mesh skinned on the same bones. Each finish has `from` and `to` (YYYY-MM), `season` (any, summer, winter), `front` (any, east, west, south, desert, pacific, china) and `share` (how common it was). Picking, for each man: the finishes whose months hold the battle's date and whose season and front fit (any fits all), one chosen by share, and face = a hash of (block id, k) mod 8 and the helmet from another hash of the same, so a man keeps both all battle. When no finish fits the date, draw the first finish (or his own helmet). No swastika, rising-sun flag or fascist badge is drawn: the German eagle decal is left off (its side stays plain paint).
about_deaths: Deaths (Tools/battle_units/falls.py on ragdoll.py): every die_* clip named in `deaths` is a physics fall baked from this man's own body (his parts' masses, his joints' human ranges, the muscle tone going out of him, the ground under him; the rifle leaves his hand and lands where it lands), so no two kinds fall alike and none sinks into the ground. Pick: deaths[stance][kind], stance stand, run, kneel, prone or cover (what he was doing when hit), kind as the Fates picker's man_fall kinds (forward, back, side, knees, spin, thrown) or crawl (wounded: he falls, drags himself on a little, then goes still), or where he was hit when the scene knows it: head (he drops where he stands), gut (he folds at the waist, then goes down), leg (that leg goes from under him); one of the list by a hash of (block id, man). Play it once (loop false) and hold its last frame for the rest of the battle: the body stays where it fell. Each clip starts in the pose of `start` [clip, time] (blend into it over ~0.15 s from whatever he was doing); `end_offset` is where his pelvis ends (metres, his own axes; the clip is not in place: the pelvis and the rifle move); the weapon bone's last key is the rifle lying on the ground. Events: knee_down, body_fall, rifle_drop (and elbow_down in a crawl), at the time they touch. The older die_back, die_forward and die_kneel stay in the file as they were but are not in the table (they sink into the ground).
about_wear: Wear and weather (Tools/battle_units/shade.py; Brian, 22 November 2026: uniforms dirtier the longer a unit is at the front, fresh replacements clean; rain darkens the cloth and splashes the mud higher; snow white on the shoulders and helmets). Per point, at near, mid and far and on each helmet finish's own mesh: `shade` (0.4 to 1) and `tint` (3 a point: red, green, blue) are the look as baked, a man some weeks in the line (wear W 0.6) in dry weather, for drawing paint x shade x tint as ever. `shade_clean`: the same shadow with no dirt (folds, under the straps, pack, belt and helmet brim, worn edges, the cloth's uneven fade). `dirt` (0 to 1): where dust and mud collect in dry weather (boots, leggings and trousers to a little over the knee in splashes, the knees, the seat, elbows, cuffs and hands, a little in the face's creases); `dirt_wet`: the same in rain (mud splashed up the thighs, caked boots, heavier knees and seat, the forearms and the front of the belly from going down in it). `wet` (0 to 1): how much the surface darkens when soaked (wool 1, webbing 0.8, leather 0.6, wood 0.45, helmet paint 0.3, steel 0.2, skin 0.15; less under the pack and the arms). `snow` (0 to 1): how much snow settles there on a man standing (open to the sky and facing up: the helmet's crown, shoulders, pack, the tops of the arms and boots; little on skin and steel). MIXING, per man: W = wear, from how long his unit has been at the front (0.1 a fresh replacement or a new unit, 1 six weeks or more in the line; replacements in a veteran unit stay low until they have been in it a while), R = rain (0 dry ground to 1 soaked) and S = snow (0 to 1), both from the battle's weather draw. In sRGB 0 to 1: base = paint x shade_clean x (1 - 0.35 x wet x R) (x the face's tone and tint); d = (dirt + (dirt_wet - dirt) x R) x W; soil = (DUST + (MUD - DUST) x R) x shade_clean, DUST (0.60, 0.54, 0.43) dry dust and dried mud, MUD (0.27, 0.21, 0.15) wet mud (or the field's own soil, lighter dry); colour = base + (soil - base) x 0.85 x d; then toward snow (0.92, 0.94, 0.97) x (0.6 + 0.4 x shade_clean) by 0.9 x snow x S. The gore paints (wound, bone, blood): shade 1, no dirt, wet or snow. Mid and far carry the near's, their shade eased off (90 % and 75 % of the darkening).

face_mesh.about: Close-range face (Tools/battle_units/face_mesh.py): the near mesh's face is split finer, red-green (no crack), and its new points set on MakeHuman's man the file was cut from (seed and nation below), so lids, lips, nostrils and the folds by the nose come back; the eyeballs' fronts are split once on their own spheres. No index moves: a split triangle keeps its place with its first piece; the other pieces and the new points are on the end of near's lists (from the first new point and triangle below), so helmet_tris and the gore ranges stay true. Each new point takes its parents' bone weights, shade, wear and tint, and in each face their move, facing and tint. Mid and far are as they were.
